title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
statement:
You're given the heads of two singly linked lists, `l1` and `l2`. Each list is already sorted from smallest to largest (equal values may repeat). Combine them into a single sorted linked list by relinking the nodes you were given, and return the head of the combined list.

Either list may be empty, in which case its head is `None`. Each node is a `ListNode` with a `val` and a `next` attribute; the class is already defined for you. In the examples, a list is written as its values from head to tail.

Constraints: each list has 0 to 50 nodes; -100 <= val <= 100.
signature: def merge_two_lists(l1: Optional[ListNode], l2: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:

examples.explanation: The two lists interleave; the equal 4s both appear.
When one list is empty, the answer is the other list.
All of l2 comes before the single node of l1.

hints: At any moment, which two nodes are the only candidates for the next spot in the merged list?
Building the head of the result is the awkward part. Is there a way to avoid special-casing the first node?
A placeholder node in front of the result, plus a pointer to the current tail, makes every step look the same.
What should happen when one list runs out before the other? Do you need to walk the rest of it?
Compare the two current heads, attach the smaller one to the tail and advance it; when one list is empty, attach the other in one step.
followUps: What are the time and space complexity, and does a recursive version change the space cost?
Is your merge stable, meaning equal values from l1 stay ahead of those from l2, and when would that matter?
How would you extend this to merge k sorted lists efficiently?
What would go wrong if one of the input lists were not actually sorted, and could you detect it cheaply?
idealAnswerPoints: Uses a dummy head and a tail pointer so the first node needs no special case
Relinks the existing nodes instead of allocating new ones
Attaches the remaining list in one step when the other runs out
States O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space, and notes recursion costs O(n + m) stack
weakAnswerSigns: Copies the values into a Python list, sorts it and builds new nodes
Loses the head of the result by advancing the only pointer to it
Walks the leftover list node by node, or drops it entirely
Crashes when either input is empty

rubric.correctness: Correctly ordered result for empty inputs, unequal lengths, duplicates and negatives, without dropping or duplicating nodes.
rubric.efficiency: O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space by relinking; recursion is fine if its stack cost is named.
rubric.code_quality: Dummy head and tail pointer, no special case for the first node, leftovers attached in one step.
rubric.communication: Describes how the pointers move before coding and checks the empty-list cases out loud.
